🔥🇲🇽 SALINAS PLIEGO'S BETTING HOUSES CAUGHT IN MONEY-LAUNDERING DRAGNET

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF), working with the US OFAC, has 39 corporate groups that control the country's casinos under investigation for laundering narco money — and has already suspended the online betting houses Ganador Azteca and Operadora Ganador TV Azteca, both owned by Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Grupo Salinas, plus casinos Centenario, Diamante, Midas and Palermo. The operations spanned Jalisco, Nuevo León, Sonora, Sinaloa and five other states.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO BETS ON PEACE THROUGH JUSTICE — NOT TANKS — IN MICHOACÁN

While Washington pushes a militarized "war on cartels," Sheinbaum's government is pouring more than 57 billion pesos into Michoacán under a plan whose stated mission is to turn the state into "a humanist and economic power" — including 37.45 billion pesos in 2026 for scholarships and Bienestar programs reaching 1.5 million people. Security built on education, health, housing and dignified work, not occupation.

🇲🇽🛢️ PEMEX AND PETROBRAS JOIN FORCES IN THE GULF — SOUTH-SOUTH ENERGY

After Lula proposed the alliance, the two state oil companies signed a two-year memorandum to cooperate on Gulf of Mexico exploration, refining, fertilizers and biofuels — pooling Petrobras's deepwater and sugarcane-biofuel tech with Pemex's fertilizer advances. Sheinbaum said the accord will "accelerate oil exploration in the Gulf of Mexico."

🇲🇽🏛️ A MAYA CITY SLEPT UNTOUCHED FOR 1,000 YEARS IN THE JUNGLE OF CAMPECHE

Archaeologists found Minanbé — "no road" in Maya — inside the Calakmul reserve: a 15-hectare city with a 13-meter pyramid and 14 carved monuments, unlooted for a millennium. Stela 1 carries the date 849 AD, just before the great regional collapse. The find caps three decades mapping a landscape that once held up to 11 million people.

🇲🇽🌉 A "WORK OF SOCIAL JUSTICE": MEXICO'S ONE-OF-A-KIND BRIDGE CUTS A 5-HOUR TRIP TO 2

Sheinbaum supervised the Rizo de Oro bridge over the Grijalva in Chiapas — 2.1 km long, a mixed-arch design unique in Mexico, with 27 segments weighing 2,730 tonnes, built by Mexican engineering. It connects 21 communities and benefits 300,000 people, cutting the trip to the capital from five hours to two.

🇲🇽🏠 MEXICO IS CANCELING THE DEBTS NEOLIBERALISM BUILT TO TRAP THE POOR

In Chiapas, Sheinbaum handed over new homes and wiped out "unpayable" credits — like Carlos Ortiz, who borrowed 89,000 pesos, paid back 446,000, and was still told he owed 1.35 million. Reviewing 5 million Infonavit/Fovissste loans from the neoliberal era has freed about 20 million Mexicans, and Vivienda para el Bienestar now adds 1% of GDP.
📸 Vivienda para el Bienestar — Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas · 28 de junio de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "How is it possible that a loan does not go down as you keep paying it?" "Because they built it to always take money from the worker." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas On Dec 31 last year, 4,856,000 "unpayable" Infonavit loans were restructured — debts that grew no matter how much workers paid. Today there is no requirement to get a home, and 75% of recipients are young people.

🇲🇽✊ 1.8 million homes. Close to 30 million people. "We are building 1 million 800 thousand homes... we are going to help close to 30 million people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas The program is already adding close to 1% of GDP to Mexico's economic growth. In Chiapas the goal is 70,000 new homes this term — over 23,000 already delivered.

🇲🇽✊ "We call ourselves humanists for one simple reason: we govern for the people." "For 36 years of neoliberalism, Infonavit stopped building homes — it handed out loans designed to keep taking the worker's money. We changed that." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas In housing it is easy to tell the difference between neoliberal governments and humanist ones. Mexico is building homes again — not debt.
